take.en: DeepSeek open-sourced the inference stack that actually runs their production models — not another toy runner.

why.en: If you ship DeepSeek at scale, the hard part is not downloading weights. It is prefill and decode throughput, MoE expert placement, draft verification, and batch-invariant results you can trust. DeepInfer is the framework DeepSeek says powers their own large-scale services, now usable offline with the same kernel and scheduling ideas.

explanation.en: DeepInfer is DeepSeek-AI's high-performance inference framework for DeepSeek models, starting with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. It packages optimized kernels (FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, DeepEP and friends), attention data-parallel and balanced context-parallel paths, MoE expert parallel with load balancing, DSpark draft verification, asynchronous zero-overhead batch scheduling, structured outputs, and optional batch-invariant plus deterministic sampling. Hardware targets are NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs. The open release focuses on offline inference; full online serving still needs your own KV cache, prefill/decode disaggregation, and replica load balancing.

howItWorks.en: On Linux with Python 3.12 and CUDA 13 (or CANN 9.2 on Ascend), set DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR, run the build script, then offline_inference.py. The default V4.1-Flash checkpoint pulls from Hugging Face on first run, or point DEEPINFER_HF_MODEL_DIR at a local path. Feature flags turn on MTP draft length, SWA bounded replay, batch-invariant mode, and grammar or JSON constrained generation. Sweep scripts in the repo reproduce the published prefill and decode Pareto charts.

different.en: This is not a laptop MoE streamer and not a generic multi-model server first. It is DeepSeek's own production-shaped runtime for their models, with the kernels and schedulers they already run at scale, released so builders can match that path instead of reverse-engineering it on top of vLLM alone.
